Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 13-May-2025 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester - End Semester Examination - April / May -2025  
  ADVANCED DATA STRUCTURE [IT-5013]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                                                                                                                       (4)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A dynamic array doubles its size whenever its capacity is full.                                        (4)  
  
  i. Analyze the time complexity of inserting nnn elements into such an array usingamortized  
  analysis.  
  ii. Compare this with the worst-case time complexity of a single insertion when resizing occurs.  
  
  Draw a conclusion about why amortized analysis is more informative in this scenario.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Provide a real-world scenario that can be modeled as an NP-Complete problem. Identify the              (2)  
  name of the problem and the challenge it presents.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                You are given the following list of integers representing task priorities:                             (4)  
  [15, 7, 20, 3, 10, 8, 12, 5, 18, 6]  
  A)  
  Page 1 of 4

1. Construct a min-heap from this array using the given order of insertion.  
  2. Then, insert three new priority values one by one: 2, 1, 9  
  
  
  After each insertion, update the array representation of the heap.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)                                                                                                           (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   A real-time system must handle tasks with different priority levels (lower number = higher priority).   (3)  
  Apply a data structure that schedules and executes the highest-priority task first.  
  Apply your structure to insert the following tasks with priorities:  
  {(TaskA, 3), (TaskB, 1), (TaskC, 2), (TaskD, 1)}  
  Show the order in which tasks will be executed.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)        Construct a 2-3 Tree by inserting the following sequence of keys:                                       (4)  
  [5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50]  
  A)   Solve the problem step-by-step and illustrate the tree after all insertions.  
  Explain how the 2-3 Tree properties (nodes with 2 or 3 children, sorted values) are preserved.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   You are given the input values to construct a binary tree (not necessarily a BST):                      (3)  
  [A, B, C, D, E, F, G]  
  Assume the tree is built in level-order. Apply post-order traversal on the tree and write the result.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Construct a Binary Search Tree by inserting the following sequence of keys:                             (3)  
  [45, 30, 60, 20, 50, 70, 10]  
  Demonstrate the final tree structure and verify that it satisfies the BST property.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)        Given the array:                                                                                        (4)  
  [32, 15, 7, 89, 42, 12, 64, 25, 19, 5, 37]  
  A)   Apply the Quick Sort algorithm using the first element as the pivot.  
  Show the recursive partitioning steps and the final sorted array.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   You are given the array:                                                                                (3)  
  [2, -4, 3, -1, 2, -5, 4, 6, -3, 2]  
  Apply the divide-and-conquer method to solve the maximum subarray sum problem.  
  
  Page 2 of 4

Break down the array into subproblems and show how the solution is built.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         You are given the following characters and their frequencies:                                           (3)  
  A (5), B (9), C (12), D (13), E (16), F (45)  
  Apply the greedy Huffman encoding strategy to build the optimal prefix code.  
  Show the process of tree construction and the final code for each character.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
5)                                                                                                                       (4)  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Evaluate the suitability of Dijkstra's Algorithm and Bellman-Ford Algorithm for finding the shortest    (4)  
  path in a weighted graph with negative edge weights.  
  Compare their time complexities and justify which algorithm is more appropriate under different  
  conditions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  C)         Identify two scenarios where using 2-3-Trees could be more beneficial than AVL trees.                   (2)  
  Mention the trade-offs in terms of rotation cost and complexity.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
